curriculumTitle: What can we do to make driving safer for everyone?
subject: Physics
centralPhenomenon: Puzzling patterns in traffic collision data - while vehicle fatalities have decreased over decades, this trend has stalled and collisions/injuries are increasing
description: Students investigate factors affecting vehicle safety including distracted driving and vehicle design, developing understanding of momentum, forces, and engineering design solutions

parts.partTitle: What factors can make driving more risky?
parts.partSubtitle: Investigating distracted driving, reaction time, and momentum

units.title: Anchoring Phenomenon and Initial Models
units.coreIdea: Vehicle collision data shows puzzling trends that need investigation through scientific and engineering approaches.
units.drivingQuestion: What can we do to make driving safer for everyone?
units.phenomenon: Analysis of traffic collision data trends and development of initial models
keyContent: Vehicle fatalities have generally decreased over decades but trend has stalled
Collisions and injuries are actually increasing
Multiple factors may contribute to vehicle safety trends
units.assessment: Pre-assessment: Initial models and Driving Question Board

units.title: Distracted Driving and Reaction Time
units.coreIdea: Distracted driving affects reaction time, which impacts stopping distance and collision risk.
units.drivingQuestion: How does distracted driving contribute to collision risk?
units.phenomenon: Video analysis of distracted vs. non-distracted drivers encountering obstacles
keyContent: Reaction time affects motion and stopping distance
Relationship between reaction time and collision risk
activities: Measurement and comparison of reaction times
units.assessment: Formative: Reaction time and stopping distance analysis

units.title: Mass, Velocity, and Momentum
units.coreIdea: Momentum, defined as mass times velocity, helps describe and predict collision outcomes.
units.drivingQuestion: How do mass and velocity affect collision outcomes?
units.phenomenon: Videos, graphs, and simulations of cart collisions with varying masses and velocities
keyContent: Momentum as a useful quantity for predicting collision outcomes

units.title: Forces, Time, and Change in Momentum
units.coreIdea: The relationship between net force, time, and change in momentum can be described mathematically through impulse.
units.drivingQuestion: How do forces over time affect momentum changes?
units.phenomenon: Cart on ramp investigations showing force-time-momentum relationships
keyContent: Quantitative relationship between net force, time, and change in momentum

units.title: Newton's Second Law and Momentum
units.coreIdea: Newton's second law (F=ma) connects forces to acceleration and can be related to momentum changes.
units.drivingQuestion: How does Newton's second law relate to momentum changes in collisions?
units.phenomenon: Mathematical analysis connecting F=ma to momentum changes
keyContent: Connection between acceleration and momentum change
Force as a vector quantity with magnitude and direction

units.title: Momentum Conservation
units.coreIdea: Momentum is conserved in a system when no net external force acts on it.
units.drivingQuestion: What happens to momentum in collision systems?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of momentum before and after collisions in isolated systems

units.title: Transfer Task - Bus Safety Analysis
units.coreIdea: Momentum and force concepts can be applied to analyze real-world transportation safety data.
units.drivingQuestion: How can we use our understanding to explain bus safety data?
units.phenomenon: Real data about bus safety compared to other vehicle types
keyContent: Application of momentum concepts to real data
Connection between vehicle mass and safety outcomes
activities: Application of momentum and force concepts

parts.partTitle: How can we make design decisions that will make driving safer in our community?
parts.partSubtitle: Engineering design solutions for vehicle safety

units.title: Collision Simulations and Force Analysis
units.coreIdea: Computer simulations can help predict how forces change over time during collisions.
units.drivingQuestion: How do forces change during a collision?
units.phenomenon: Gizmo simulation creating collision timelines for crash-test dummies and vehicles
keyContent: Force changes over time during collisions

units.title: Safety Features Investigation
units.coreIdea: Safety features like crumple zones, seat belts, and airbags reduce peak forces by extending contact time.
units.drivingQuestion: How do safety features affect collision forces?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of how specific safety features modify collision forces
keyContent: Extended contact time reduces force magnitude
activities: Force measurement with and without safety features

units.title: Crumple Zone Design Analysis
units.coreIdea: The rigidity and length of crumple zones significantly impact occupant safety during collisions.
units.drivingQuestion: How do crumple zone properties affect occupant safety?
units.phenomenon: Analysis of crumple zone rigidity and length effects on collision outcomes
keyContent: Relationship between crumple zone properties and safety

units.title: Vehicle Design Optimization
units.coreIdea: Vehicle design requires balancing multiple criteria including safety, cost, mass, and societal impacts.
units.drivingQuestion: How can we optimize vehicle designs for safety while considering constraints?
units.phenomenon: Comprehensive vehicle design considering mass-related tradeoffs and societal issues
keyContent: Societal and ethical implications of design decisions
Cost, safety, reliability, and environmental impacts
units.assessment: Summative: Community Design Solution (culminating engineering task)

units.title: Community-Relevant Safety Issues
units.coreIdea: Local driving safety issues require research-based solutions that consider community-specific factors.
units.drivingQuestion: What driving safety issues are most relevant to our community?
units.phenomenon: Research into local driving safety challenges and solution development

units.title: Community Design Solutions
units.coreIdea: Effective community safety solutions require consideration of human and environmental values across multiple scales.
units.drivingQuestion: How can we propose effective safety solutions for our community?
units.phenomenon: Development and presentation of community-specific safety design solutions
units.assessment: Formative: Community Design Solution presentations and peer feedback

units.title: Transfer Task - Historical Design Solutions
units.coreIdea: Historical design solutions can be evaluated using modern understanding of physics and engineering principles.
units.drivingQuestion: How do historical safety solutions compare to modern approaches?
units.phenomenon: Comparison of vintage pedestrian design solutions using current understanding
keyContent: Application of physics principles to evaluate past designs
activities: Physics principle application to historical context

disciplinary_core_ideas: PS2.A - Forces and Motion (momentum, Newton's second law)
ETS1.A - Defining and Delimiting Engineering Problems

mathematical_requirements: Applying geometric methods to design problems
Interpreting slope and intercept of linear models

summative: Community Design Solution (culminating engineering task, Lesson 11)

social_emotional_considerations.trauma_informed_approach: Vehicle collisions can be traumatic - teachers advised to consult school counselors and send pre-unit letters home
social_emotional_considerations.equity_focus: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) integration for equitable access
social_emotional_considerations.socio_ecological_framework: Learning in Places framework for considering human and environmental values in decision-making
